title: Unit build alternatives and their board conditions

cases.title: AP-oriented Nidalee within comparable boards
cases.subject: units
cases.original_question: Are AP builds on two-star Nidalee competitive with AD builds, or do they only hold up on certain boards?
cases.question: Are AP builds on two-star Nidalee competitive with AD builds, or do they only hold up on certain boards?
cases.scenario: Nidalee2 with exactly three ordinary items, partitioning explicit AP-oriented, AD-oriented and mixed triplets; compare within observed cores and Invoker strata.
cases.plan: rank_unit_loadouts discovers actual exact trios; use the item catalogue to declare a reproducible orientation taxonomy. compare_cohorts contrasts named triplets within shared supports and trait contribution intervals. query_cohort/deltas discovers the allied package, with entity names retained in grouped rows.
cases.checks: Keep mixed/ambiguous trios separate and show support/outcomes for each compared package. Investigate whether differences persist inside named contexts, not only aggregate AP/AD labels. No fixed preferred build or ranking is expected.
cases.limits: No AP/AD filter or observed Adaptor-form field exists. A named item-based orientation proxy must be explicit and must not be called confirmed ranged/melee form. Other inventory and global investment remain residual confounders.

cases.title: Azir’s Shojin slot
cases.subject: units
cases.original_question: Does three-star Azir need Shojin, or can I build Guinsoo’s plus two damage items? Are there boards where spending that slot on mana looks more worthwhile?
cases.question: Does three-star Azir need Shojin, or can I build Guinsoo’s plus two damage items? Are there boards where spending that slot on mana looks more worthwhile?
cases.scenario: Azir3 with Guinsoo's, one shared named damage item, and either Shojin or a second named damage item, ordinary three-item trios only.
cases.plan: Discover exact fixed-pair loadouts, classify the second damage item without assuming all damage items lack mana benefits, and compare explicit holder trios. Repeat in supported Blackthorn/Executioner/Summoner contribution contexts and named frontline shells.
cases.checks: Preserve Guinsoo's and the shared item, report exact third-slot cells with counts/mean/top4/win and available intervals. Explain board-context variation from crossed observations, not a mana theory alone.
cases.limits: No mana-generation/combat simulator gold. Additional damage-item definitions are preparation choices; total board-item equality and Blackthorn sacrifice are not enforceable.

cases.title: Rapidfire-emblem Nidalee as an exceptional build
cases.subject: units
cases.original_question: Does AP Nidalee with a Rapidfire emblem actually outperform ordinary AP builds, or is it mainly showing up on much stronger endgame boards?
cases.question: Does AP Nidalee with a Rapidfire emblem actually outperform ordinary AP builds, or is it mainly showing up on much stronger endgame boards?
cases.scenario: Nidalee2 with Rapidfire Emblem plus two declared AP-oriented ordinary items versus the same pair plus each observed ordinary third; three items on one holder.
cases.plan: Discover ordinary pairs and emblem loadouts, then compare exact holder-bound packages within supported Rapidfire contribution and allied-core strata. Query final level, board item count, frontline upgrades and other carry loadouts as comparability diagnostics.
cases.checks: Bind the emblem to Nidalee and preserve the shared pair. Show cell samples/outcomes and whether support differs across observed packages. Do not use emblem-wide or Nidalee-wide averages as the exact build comparison.
cases.limits: AP orientation is an item-defined proxy, not guaranteed form. Emblem source and complete board wealth cannot be controlled with current tools; residual selection may explain outcome gaps.

cases.title: Ahri double Blue Buff outside the simulator
cases.subject: units
cases.original_question: A simulator suggested double Blue Buff for Ahri. Do two-star Ahri endgame boards with that build actually hold up against a single mana item and two damage items, and does the surrounding board change the comparison?
cases.question: A simulator suggested double Blue Buff for Ahri. Do two-star Ahri endgame boards with that build actually hold up against a single mana item and two damage items, and does the surrounding board change the comparison?
cases.scenario: Ahri2: two ordinary Blue Buff copies plus a shared damage item versus one Blue Buff plus that item and another damage item. Shojin alternatives are separate.
cases.plan: Resolve Blue Buff and query rank_unit_loadouts with duplicate required item terms: distinct-slot matching supports multiplicity discovery. If the chosen scope/reference permits and records this inventory, compare exact single-copy Ahri trios using explicit item multiplicity and per-holder item count. Split Blossom/Spellweaver/Invoker contexts.
cases.checks: Verify two copies, not the same item condition repeated twice with default one-copy semantics. Preserve the shared damage item and star level, show counts/outcomes, and report an empty/suppressed build distinctly from an illegality conclusion.
cases.limits: The local catalogue does not establish Blue Buff uniqueness/stacking legality for 18.3B. Do not invent a rule or fabricate sample support; record legality/reference uncertainty while still performing supported discovery. The simulator is motivation, not an expected result.
